newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia takeover bill becomes law.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia takeover bill becomes law.

text.p: Slovenia's parliament passed a disputed takeover law on Tuesday, overruling an earlier veto by the upper house State Council.
The legislation, which now enters the statute book, gives state watchdog the Securities Market Agency jurisdiction over some corporate acquisitions.
Parliament first approved the takeover law on July 1. Then the State Council exercised its one veto, arguing the changes put small shareholders at a disadvantage.
After the second reading, parliament voted 74-0 in favour of the law, easily exceeding the required simple majority in Slovenia's 90-seat assembly.

According to the law, the Securities Market Agency will oversee purchases involving more than 25 percent of shares of listed companies or those with at least one billion tolars ($5.9 million) in equity capital.
It also applies to companies with over 500 shareholders.
In the case of newly-privatised companies, the government must approve purchases involving more than 25 percent of shares in firms whose equity capital exceeds 800 million tolars.
It is Slovenia's first takeover legislation. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439 ($ = 168.6 Slovenian Tolars)
